# Copilot Instructions

## Repository Overview

This repository contains Prometheus alert rules, their unit tests, and textfile collector scripts for node exporter.

## Repository Structure

```
.
├── rules/                  # Prometheus alert rule files (YAML)
├── tests/                  # promtool unit tests for the rules (YAML)
├── textfile-collector/     # Shell scripts for node_exporter textfile collector
├── .pint.hcl               # pint lint configuration
├── Makefile                # Test and lint targets
└── README.md
```

## Alert Rule Files (`rules/`)

Each file in `rules/` is a valid Prometheus rule file. Files are named after the component or system they monitor (e.g., `cpu.yml`, `disk.yml`, `mysql.yml`).

### Structure

```yaml
---
groups:
  - name: <GroupName>
    rules:
      - alert: <AlertName>
        expr: <PromQL expression>
        for: <duration>
        labels:
          severity: <page|warning|info>
        annotations:
          summary: <short description (instance {{ $labels.instance }})>
          description: "<detailed description>\n  VALUE = {{ $value }}\n  LABELS = {{ $labels }}"
```

### Conventions

- Alert names use `CamelCase`.
- Group names are lowercase (matching the filename without extension), except where a proper noun is used.
- Severity labels are one of: `page`, `warning`, `info`. Never use `critical` or `error`: they are not routed. `none` is reserved for the always-firing dead man's switch.
- Every alert has a `summary` annotation.
- Tiered alerts (a warning and a page on the same metric) use exclusive ranges so one problem raises one alert, e.g. `> 80 <= 90` for the warning and `> 90` for the page.
- Annotations may only reference labels the expression keeps. After `sum by (job)`, `absent()`, `vector()` or `count()`, `{{ $labels.instance }}` is empty: reference the labels in `by (...)` instead.
- Do not edit `mimir-alerts.yml` / `mimir-rules.yml` by hand: they are generated by the upstream Grafana Mimir mixin and excluded from `make lint`.
- PromQL expressions that use node metrics typically enrich with hostname using:
  ```
  * on(instance) group_left (nodename) node_uname_info{nodename=~".+"}
  ```
- Wrap the main expression in parentheses before the enrichment join.
- `summary` annotations follow the pattern: `<Human readable description> (instance {{ $labels.instance }})`.
- `description` annotations include `VALUE = {{ $value }}` and `LABELS = {{ $labels }}`.

## Textfile Collector Scripts (`textfile-collector/`)

Shell scripts intended to be used with [node_exporter's textfile collector](https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter#textfile-collector). Scripts must pass `shellcheck`.

## Development Workflow

### Run tests (validates all rule files and runs the unit tests using `promtool`)

```sh
make test
```

This runs `promtool check rules` on all files in `rules/`, then `promtool test rules` on all files in `tests/`, via Docker.

### Lint rules with pint

```sh
make lint
```

This runs `pint` in offline mode with `.pint.hcl`. Only `Bug` findings fail; fix them rather than silencing them.

### Run shellcheck on textfile-collector scripts

```sh
make shellcheck
```

### Add a new alert rule

1. Add or edit the appropriate YAML file in `rules/`.
2. Add or update a unit test in `tests/` (`rule_files: [../rules/<file>.yml]`, `input_series`, `alert_rule_test`). Include a case the previous expression got wrong when fixing a rule.
3. Run `make test lint`.
4. Follow the existing structure: `groups` → `rules` → `alert`, `expr`, `for`, `labels`, `annotations`.

## Git Commit Messages

All commits must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification.

### Format

```
<type>[optional scope]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

### Types

| Type       | When to use                                               |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feat`     | A new alert rule or textfile collector script             |
| `fix`      | A bug fix in an existing rule or script                   |
| `docs`     | Documentation changes only (README, comments, etc.)      |
| `style`    | Formatting changes that do not affect meaning             |
| `refactor` | Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature   |
| `test`     | Adding or updating tests                                  |
| `chore`    | Maintenance tasks (CI config, Makefile, dependencies)     |

### Examples

```
feat(rules): add HostOomKillDetected alert
fix(rules): correct threshold for HostHighCpuLoad
docs: update README with new alert descriptions
chore(ci): update promtool Docker image version
```
